newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - CORPORATE LLOYD'S.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - CORPORATE LLOYD'S.

text.p: Lloyd's of London received two votes of confidence this week. One from Commercial Union's decision to buy a majority stake in one of the insurance market's member firms, Marlborough Underwriting Agency Ltd. The other from Bermuda-based Mid Ocean's announcement to buy out the remainder of another managing agency, Brockbank.

The first is significant because CU is the first big British insurer to take control of a Lloyd's underwriting unit. It is all the more significant because CU is regarded as perhaps the most cautious of Britain's big non-life insurers.
So, its decision to buy a Lloyd's underwriter probably tells us more about the state of the Lloyd's market than Monday's qualified auditor's report on Equitas, the Lloyd's reinsurance vehicle.
Mid Ocean's move underlines the strong support shown by Bermuda ever since Lloyd's opened up to corporate investors in 1994.

It also demonstrates that the insurance market has probably changed more in the last three years than in the previous three centuries, when Lloyd's relied solely on individual investors for capital backing.
As big insurers move in to snap up most of Lloyd's managing agencies, it looks increasingly as if the market's 160 or so insurance syndicates will become more like small insurance companies.

Many believe that this could spell the end of the entrepreneurial spirit of the individual Lloyd's underwriter and radically alter the nature of the market, which could be left providing little more than branding and support services.
